newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea govt not to intervene to save Kia Group.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea govt not to intervene to save Kia Group.

text.p: South Korean Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik said the government has no plans to intervene to save the struggling Kia Group, senior ministry officials said on Thursday.

"The government has no plans to support an individual company through such measures as debt guarantees and loans from the government at the expense of the public," Kang was quoted by the officials as telling President Kim Young-sam on Wednesday.
Kang also was quoted as saying the matter of giving soft loans through the Central Bank of Korea to Kia's main creditor Korea First Bank would be considered more carefully.
He said he was worried about the impact of such loans on price stability and the possibility that such loans would be regarded as preferential treatment for Korea First Bank.
Kia's 18 affiliates were selected for protection by creditor banks last week after the group was determined unable to avoid defaulting on its debt payments.
